leverage.exposure: This is the figure that matters most and it is the one to watch. The two live bids together commit substantially more than the cash on hand. If both land, the balance goes deeply negative and the squad goes to thirteen; clearing it means executing both sales, which restores a small positive balance and returns the squad to eleven. If only the midfielder lands, one sale clears it and the defender's sale becomes void. If only the defender lands, the other sale clears it and the midfielder's sale becomes void — selling both would drop the squad to ten. The estimates behind every branch assume one market-value tick before the lock, and both sale candidates are falling, so their proceeds will be slightly lower by then; every branch still clears with margin, but the margin is not large and a missed unwind means a zero-point matchday across the whole eleven. Nothing is leveraged right now — the balance is positive — but it will be within a day if the auctions go the way the bids intend.

binding_gap: There is no positional hole. The binding constraint is the eleven-man floor itself, combined with the three-defender minimum. Nothing can be sold before something is bought, and the weakest fielded body is a sub-thirty-average defender who cannot be sold at all without a defender landing first. The upgrade targets are therefore the two weakest midfield and defensive returns, not a gap in the shape.
